## India: DPDPA Implementation and Regulatory Developments

MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan confirmed that there will be no extension for startups to comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), signaling a firm timeline for implementation. This comes as various government ministries and state bodies are actively assessing their readiness for the sweeping data compliance requirements introduced by the Act. ([Source](https://news.google.?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

MeitY has also initiated the operationalization of the Data Protection Board by inviting applications for its Chairperson and members. This critical step will establish the independent body responsible for enforcing the DPDPA and adjudicating violations. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivwFBVV95cUxPMTJ3Q0xjOXBlWVRYRGVtamRYWUg3VGFUQ2UwLXlqbVFBaXNfcFhfV3piMEYxdkpmZnlGQ28yTWlyY18zYk42UGhhOHBKTVB6bXRobjZfMWJfVVRLd1N2OU9acjBIQmVScGRkSFBlR2xmRGV0T3NKYzlBVFRKUUlKNzFVd3k4WWt3cC04NXhTejgzRnJCcUVITzFOenAwRk9GbXVpMEZxbjJMai1DZ1pKSDMyZ2pSQXJfUDBMWnF2OA?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.?oc=5))

## DPDPA's Broad Impact and Key Challenges

The DPDPA is poised to significantly reshape data handling across various sectors, including EdTech, Med-Tech, and Global Capability Centres (GCCs), requiring them to adapt to new consent management frameworks and data fiduciary responsibilities. The Act's intersection with artificial intelligence (AI) is also a growing focus, with cases like ANI v. OpenAI highlighting the need for clear guidelines on data processing for AI development. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxNLS1IMzByRTNKS0g1R0ZuX2ItZW1PaWJyaG11NEVrZ2FUQklNYUxCWFBlTnk0Q2V0ZnNwSXpFRE1pUklTdFdLUUtrd211QTl0LVd6Q0IzekFKLTRmTFowX0hUNkJrVXFOR2pwNXM2dENwR19PLWJXQUFpblZRLTBtcmIzR3VDTWhxQWRhLV9qQy1kSl93dVl3OTg1a09waVhneUhQMm9SWEJFS0RZNm5EaUdiYUNyVlJZUjc0M3gxU096OVpCcDBBZA?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxObkVMMTdUWFlaOVY3NkJISkpSR0ZQdEtpT3NoMDczZ2lPUHNnOGYyTDJEX1daTVdyeGxiNEZxQnhTeFdEb2tsZkJMekRlbU9VUkpMY1pfQmxpT2dWRzkzTUc5V1NKTWFpZWdMUWtRYk1XTXIxVk9Fak5heGRtZWtONS1qaXBGUlpFSVJ4dmNkRENPaEVHaXRab0d5QXZTSmNL?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.?oc=5), [Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxPbU1sYkRyai1qeW44bzdJVUlDX0cyTmgzdThLbThUc29qa2otT2lDdnZVV2Vpa29HSWNYeDlGTnZpeTh0MGFKWEJwOVpxX0dScC1KMDdoR3k4c2IxSExxUUJuVGNYbXFTaWFuWXFJWWFtcVdmTWlILU9kdmIzUnJuREpQak15WTcyOHZzazE4N2VPVHlrZmhXVU1HU3RlTG0y?oc=5))

A key interpretational challenge under the DPDPA is the absence of a statutory definition for "harm," which could lead to uncertainty in privacy adjudication. Furthermore, the Supreme Court has asked MeitY to examine a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking the recovery or destruction of Indian citizens' stolen personal data held on foreign servers, highlighting ongoing concerns about data sovereignty and breach response.
